title: C482/613/2022 of MUKARRAM Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Criminal Miscellaneous Application No. 613 of 2022
Mukarram ...... Petitioner
Vs.
State of Uttarakhand and Others ..... Respondents
Mr. Rajveer Singh, Advocate for the petitioner.
Mr. Lalit Miglani, A.G.A. for the State of Uttarakhand.

JUDGMENT
Hon'ble Ravindra Maithani, J. (Oral)
 Challenge in this petition is made to the
order dated 20.04.2022 passed in Special Sessions Trial
No. 06 of 2020, State of Uttarakhand Vs. Mukarram,
passed by learned Special Sessions Judge, Chamoli,
Gopeshwar, District Chamoli ("the case"). By the
impugned order, an application under Section 311 of the
Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (for short, "the Code")
for further examination of PW1, father of the victim and
PW2, the victim has been rejected.
2. Heard learned counsel for the parties and
perused the record.
3. According to the prosecution, the victim, a
girl aged 17 years, was found missing from her house on
11.02.2022. An FIR was lodged that it is the petitioner,

2
who had enticed the victim. After investigation,
chargesheet was submitted and proceedings of the case
initiated under Section 363, 376 IPC read with Section
3/4 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences,
2012 (for short, "the Act"). At the stage of examination of
the petitioner, under Section 313 of the Code, an
application under Section 311 of the Code was moved for
recalling PW1, the father of the victim and PW2, the
victim for their further cross-examination. It is this
application, which has been rejected by the impugned
order dated 20.04.2022.
4. Learned counsel for the petitioner would
submit that certain important questions with regard to
nikahnama could not be asked from PW1, the father of
the victim and PW2, the victim, which are necessary for
the just decision of the case. Therefore, the application
filed by the petitioner, under Section 311 of the Code,
ought to have been allowed, but the court below
committed an error in rejecting this application.
5. Learned counsel for the petitioner would
submit that, in fact, the victim is married wife of the
petitioner. Their marriage was solemnized on 10.02.2020
and on the same date, nikahnama was also executed. It

3
is argued that the nikahnama is in the custody of the
father of the victim. Therefore, on nikahnama and
marriage of the victim with the petitioner, questions are
required to be asked.
6. On the other hand, learned counsel for the
State would submit that, at a very belated stage, the
application, under Section 311 of the Code had been
moved just to delay the trial. The impugned order is in
accordance with law. It does not warrant any
interference.
7. The impugned order is quite in detail. The
court below has considered each aspect of the argument
as advanced and while examining the law on the subject,
dismissed the application.
8. Section 33 of the Act, requires that the
Special Court would ensure that the child is not called
repeatedly to testify in the court. Section 35 of the Act
provides time limit within which the trial is expected to
be concluded. But then, Section 311 of the Code has its
own scope, which permits for recalling a witness, if his
evidence appears to be essential for the just decision of
the case. But, it is also settled law that this provision

4
should not be allowed to be used for delaying the trial or
for defeating the ends of justice.
9. The application under Section 311 of the
Code was filed by the petitioner on the ground that a
new lawyer has been engaged by the petitioner. When
the new lawyer prepared for the argument, he indicated
that certain questions should have been asked from
PW1, the father of the victim and PW2, the victim. The
impugned order records that, in fact, the application was
signed by the lawyer, who had cross-examined the
witnesses.
10. PW1, the father of the victim was examined
on 03.09.2020 and PW2, the victim was also examined
on the same date. They have stated that the date of birth
of the victim is 03.02.2002. According to them, the
victim was below 18 years of age on the date of incident.
The witnesses have not been suggested that the victim is
legally wedded wife of the petitioner. In fact, in Page 6 at
Paragraph 2 of the statement of the victim, a suggestion
was given to the victim that in order to get marry the
petitioner, he has been falsely implicated. The victim
denied all these suggestions.

5
11. In the application under Section 311 of the
Code, it is not stated by the petitioner that he and the
victim were married and questions relating to the
nikahnama were to be asked. In paragraph 7 of the
impugned order, the court below has given history of the
case. In the case, the prosecution had closed evidence
on 27.07.2021. Eight dates were fixed for the defence
evidence but the petitioner did not adduce any evidence.
Finally, an endorsement was made on behalf of the
petitioner that he does not intend to adduce any
evidence in his defence. But, thereafter, the application
under Section 311 of the Code was moved.
12. Change of counsel is not a ground to recall
a witness. There cannot be many set of questions that
may be asked from a witness. Depending upon
experience, skill, knowledge, wisdom etc., of a lawyer,
questions may be formulated and asked in cross-examination of a witness. If change of lawyer is
permitted to be made a ground for recalling a witness,
this process will be endless.
13. The grounds on which application under
Section 311 of the Code has been filed for further cross-examination of PW1, the father of the victim and PW2,

6
the victim are no ground for permitting further cross
examination. The grounds, which have been taken
before this Court are, in fact, not the grounds, which
were taken in the court below. As stated, the factum of
marriage between the petitioner and the victim has never
been suggested to the father of the victim or the victim.
14. In view of the foregoing discussion, this
Court is of the view that there are no reasons to make
any interference in the matter. The impugned order is in
accordance with law. Accordingly, the petition deserves
to be dismissed at the stage of admission itself.
15. The petition is dismissed in limine.
 (Ravindra Maithani, J.)
 11.05.2022
